source_text:
Στίχ. ζ΄. Καὶ κυριεύσει ἐθνῶν πολλῶν. (25) Εἰσὶ δὲ κύριοι πολλοὶ, καὶ θεοὶ πολλοί. Μακάριοι δὲ οἱ τὸν Κύριον ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν ἔχοντες κύριον· κυριεύσουσι γὰρ κυρίας πολλάς.
Στίχ. ιζ΄. Καὶ ἀναστήσεται ἄνθρωπος ἐξ Ἰσραήλ. Φασὶ τὸν Βαλαὰμ ἔχειν φοιτητὰς τῇ τέχνῃ, μαθητεύσαντας αὐτῷ τῇ μαγικῇ· καὶ δόξαν περὶ αὐτοῦ (26), ἀναγράψασθαι τὰς προφητείας αὐτοῦ, καὶ καταλιπεῖν, ἐν αἷς καὶ τό· Ἀνατελεῖ ἄστρον. Ἤ καὶ ἐκ τῆς πατρικῆς παραδόσεως τοῦτο καὶ διαδοχῆς παραλαβόντες οἱ Μάγοι, ἐπὶ τὴν Βηθλεὲμ παρεγένοντο.
thought_title: Balaam's prophecy of a ruler and the Magi's tradition
orientation: Origen is commenting on Balaam's prophecy in Numbers, first on the ruler over many nations, then on the star prophecy and the tradition that the Magi inherited Balaam's prophecies.
pass_a_gloss: Verse 7. And he will rule over many nations. (25) But there are many lords and many gods. But blessed are those who have our Lord Jesus Christ as lord; for they will rule over many dominions. Verse 17. And a man from Israel shall rise. They say that Balaam had disciples in the art, who were instructed by him in magic; and that they had a reputation about him (26), that they wrote down his prophecies and left them behind, among which also this: A star shall rise. Or also, having received this from the ancestral tradition and succession, the Magi came to Bethlehem.

choices.english: he will rule over many nations
choices.why: The verb κυριεύω takes a genitive object; 'rule over' captures the force of lordship over nations.
rejected: he will be lord of many nations

choices.why: κυρία is a feminine noun meaning 'dominion' or 'lordship'; rendering as 'dominions' preserves the noun form rather than converting to a verb phrase.

choices.english: a man from Israel shall rise
choices.why: The glossary specifies 'a man from Israel' for ἄνθρωπος ἐξ Ἰσραήλ; 'shall rise' reflects the future middle of ἀνίστημι.
rejected: a ruler from Israel will arise

choices.why: The brief marks this as reported tradition introduced by 'they say'; the present tense is preserved.
The glossary specifies 'a star shall rise' for Ἀνατελεῖ ἄστρον.
πατρικός means 'ancestral' or 'of the fathers'; 'ancestral tradition' captures the inherited nature of the knowledge.

bible_refs.note: ἀναστήσεται ἄνθρωπος ἐξ Ἰσραήλ and Ἀνατελεῖ ἄστρον

pass_b_english: Verse 7. And he will rule over many nations (Numbers 24:7). There are indeed many lords and many gods, but blessed are those who have our Lord Jesus Christ as Lord, for they will rule over many dominions.

Verse 17. And a man from Israel shall rise (Numbers 24:17). They say that Balaam had disciples in his art, men who had been instructed by him in magic, and that they held an opinion about him and wrote down his prophecies and left them behind, including the one that says, "A star shall rise." It was through receiving this from ancestral tradition and succession that the Magi came to Bethlehem.
